subtitle: Forty verses in praise of Hanumān

epigraph.deva: यत्र यत्र रघुनाथकीर्तनं तत्र तत्र कृतमस्तकाञ्जलिम् ।
epigraph.en: Wherever the glory of Rāma is sung, there Hanumān stands, palms joined above his head.

about.heading: The Hymn
body: The *Hanumān Chālīsā* is perhaps the most widely recited hymn in the Hindu world. Its name comes from *cālīs*, 'forty', for its forty chaupāīs (quatrain verses), framed by two dohas at the beginning and one at the end.

It is written in Awadhi, the everyday speech of the region around Ayodhya, not in Sanskrit. This was a deliberate choice of its poet: to bring the love of Rāma and Hanumān into the language of ordinary people. Children learn it by heart, families recite it at dusk, and millions turn to it in moments of fear.

about.heading: The Poet: Goswami Tulsidas
body: Tulsidas (c. 1532–1623) was a poet-saint and the author of the *Rāmcharitmānas*, the Awadhi retelling of the Rāmāyaṇa that he began in Ayodhya on Rāma Navamī of 1574 and that remains the most beloved scripture of North India.

Tradition holds that he was born at Rajapur on the Yamuna and given the name *Rāmbolā* because, instead of crying at birth, he uttered 'Rāma'. Separated from his parents in infancy, he was raised in poverty and later taken in by the ascetic Narharidās, who taught him the story of Rāma.

He married Ratnāvalī and loved her intensely. The story goes that when he followed her to her father's house one stormy night, she rebuked him: 'If you had for Śrī Rāma even half the love you have for this body of bone and skin, you would be free of all fear of the world.' The words pierced him. He renounced home and gave his life to Rāma.

He spent his later years in Varanasi, where he founded the Saṅkaṭ Mochan Hanumān temple and died at Assi Ghat in 1623. His other works include the *Vinaya Patrikā*, *Kavitāvalī*, *Gītāvalī*, *Dohāvalī* and the *Hanumān Bāhuk*.

about.heading: How Tulsidas met Hanumān
body: Tradition says that in Varanasi a grateful spirit told Tulsidas that Hanumān came every day, disguised as an old leper, to listen to the Rāmāyaṇa recitation, always the first to arrive and the last to leave. Tulsidas followed the old man into the forest and fell at his feet. Hanumān revealed himself and promised him a vision of Rāma at Chitrakoot.

At Chitrakoot, as Tulsidas was grinding sandalwood paste, a young prince asked him for a tilak. Hanumān, as a parrot, sang out so that Tulsidas would recognise who stood before him: *'Chitrakūṭa ke ghāṭa para, bhai santana kī bhīra; Tulasidāsa candana ghiseṁ, tilaka deta Raghubīra'*, 'At the ghat of Chitrakoot the saints have gathered; Tulsidas grinds sandalwood, and Rāma himself applies the tilak.'

about.heading: The Legend of Fatehpur Sikri
body: A popular legend says the Chālīsā was composed in captivity. Emperor Akbar summoned Tulsidas and demanded a miracle. When the saint replied that he knew no miracle but the name of Rāma, he was imprisoned at Fatehpur Sikri. There he composed the forty verses, and when he finished, an army of monkeys overran the fort until the emperor released him with apologies.

No historical record confirms this story, and it is told as devotional legend. Tradition attributes the Chālīsā to Tulsidas, and its fortieth verse carries his name, but historians note that its authorship, like that of several shorter works linked to him, rests on tradition rather than early manuscripts.

about.heading: Language and Metre
body: The hymn uses two metres beloved in medieval Hindi poetry. The **dohā** is a couplet whose halves have 13 + 11 mātrās (syllabic beats). The **chaupāī** has four quarters of 16 mātrās each. In the Chālīsā, each chaupāī is printed as two lines.

Awadhi often softens Sanskrit words: *yaśas* becomes *jasu*, *varṇa* becomes *baran*, *vidyā* becomes *bidyā*. The word-by-word glosses on this page trace each word back to its Sanskrit root (*dhātu*, shown with √) where there is one.

about.heading: Who is Hanumān?
body: Son of Añjanā and Kesarī, and born by the blessing of Vāyu, the Wind, Hanumān is the greatest devotee in the Rāmāyaṇa. He is strong enough to leap the ocean and humble enough to want nothing but service. He is honoured as an avatāra of Śiva, a master of grammar and music, and a *cirañjīvī*, one who remains on earth through the ages.

He is the ideal of *dāsya bhakti*, love expressed as service. Asked once who he was, he is said to have answered: 'When I identify with the body, I am Your servant. As a soul, I am a part of You. In truth, You and I are one.'

about.heading: How it is recited
body: Tuesdays and Saturdays are especially sacred to Hanumān, as is Hanumān Jayantī. Many people recite the Chālīsā once each morning or evening. In times of difficulty they recite it 7, 11 or 21 times, and as a vow 100 times (as verse 38 suggests) or 108 times, the number of beads on a mala.
This page's **Recite** mode shows one verse at a time in large type and keeps count of your recitations.

about.heading: Did you know?
body: The first doha is the same as the opening doha of the Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa of the *Rāmcharitmānas*.
The 2011 T-Series video, sung by Hariharan, became the first Indian video on YouTube to pass **5 billion views** (November 2025).
Neem Karoli Baba's devotees brought the Chālīsā to the West. Ram Dass and Krishna Das made it part of kirtan gatherings around the world.
The name *Hanumān* is usually explained from *hanu*, 'jaw': the child's jaw was struck by Indra's thunderbolt when he leapt to swallow the sun (verse 18).

audio.artist: Sri Raman Bihari Das Babaji and devotees

lines.deva: श्रीगुरु चरन सरोज रज निज मनु मुकुरु सुधारि ।
lines.roman: Shri-Guru charan saroj raj, nij manu mukuru sudhari

words.root: śrī (radiance, auspiciousness; √śri, to shine) + guru (weighty, venerable; √gṝ). Traditionally explained as gu, darkness + ru, remover
Skt. saro-ja, 'born in a lake': saras (lake) + ja (√jan, to be born)

lines.deva: बरनउँ रघुबर बिमल जसु जो दायकु फल चारि ॥
lines.roman: Baranau Raghubar bimal jasu, jo dayaku phal chari

words.root: Skt. varṇayāmi ← √varṇ, to depict, to colour

words.gloss: best of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma
words.root: raghu (the Raghu dynasty) + vara (best; √vṛ, to choose)
Skt. phala ← √phal, to ripen, bear fruit

meaning.en: Cleansing the mirror of my mind with the pollen-dust of my revered Guru's lotus feet, I sing the spotless glory of Śrī Rāma, best of the Raghus, which grants the four fruits of life: dharma (righteousness), artha (wealth), kāma (fulfilment) and mokṣa (liberation).

bhava.en: The hymn begins not with Hanumān but with humility. The mind is a mirror; only when the Guru's grace wipes away its dust can it reflect the Divine. Even Hanumān's praise starts at the Guru's feet.

notes: This doha is identical to the opening doha of the Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa of Tulsidas' Rāmcharitmānas.
The 'four fruits' (puruṣārthas) are dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa.

words.root: buddhi (√budh, to awaken, to know) + hīna (√hā, to abandon)
pavana (wind, purifier; √pū, to purify) + kumāra (son, youth)

lines.deva: बल बुधि बिद्या देहु मोहिं हरहु कलेस बिकार ॥
lines.roman: Bal budhi bidya dehu mohi, harahu kales bikar

words.root: Skt. vikāra: vi + √kṛ, to make (a change, a deformity)

meaning.en: Knowing myself to be lacking in understanding, I remember you, O Son of the Wind. Grant me strength, wisdom and knowledge, and take away my afflictions and impurities.

bhava.en: An honest prayer: 'I do not know enough.' Strength (bala), wisdom (buddhi) and knowledge (vidyā) are asked for together, because each needs the others. Strength without wisdom harms, and knowledge without strength cannot act.

notes: Kleśa is a technical word in yoga: Patañjali names five kleśas, which are ignorance, ego, attachment, aversion and clinging to life.

words.root: Skt. sāgara, the ocean dug by the sons of King Sagara
Skt. loka ← √lok, to see (the visible world)
possibly from Skt. ud + √jāgṛ, to be fully awake or manifest

meaning.en: Victory to you, Hanumān, ocean of knowledge and virtue! Victory to the Lord of the monkeys, who illumines all three worlds!

bhava.en: An ocean cannot be measured or emptied, and is never diminished by those who draw from it. So it is with his wisdom and goodness.

words.root: Skt. rāma ← √ram, to delight: 'the one in whom all delight'
a (not) + √tul, to weigh: 'that cannot be weighed'

meaning.en: You are Rāma's messenger, the home of matchless strength, known as Añjanī's son and the Son of the Wind.

bhava.en: His first title is not 'mighty one' but 'Rāma's messenger'. His strength matters because it is placed in service.

words.gloss: Bajrangī, whose limbs are like the thunderbolt

words.root: Skt. nivāraṇa: ni + √vṛ, to ward off

meaning.en: Great hero, mighty in valour, with a body hard as the thunderbolt, you dispel bad thinking and are the companion of good sense.

bhava.en: He does more than remove our wrong thoughts; he stays as the friend of right thinking. Devotion is a companionship, not a one-time rescue.

words.root: Skt. vi + √rāj, to shine, to reign

meaning.en: Your golden form shines in beautiful attire, with rings in your ears and curly hair.

bhava.en: After his strength, Tulsidas lingers over his beauty. In bhakti, the Lord's form is something to gaze on lovingly, not merely to describe.

meaning.en: In your hands shine the thunderbolt and the banner, and a sacred thread of muñja grass adorns your shoulder.

bhava.en: The weapon and the sacred thread appear together: power and purity, the warrior and the seeker in one form.

notes: The banner (dhvaja) is said to be Rāma's own flag, carried by his foremost servant. Arjuna's chariot in the Mahābhārata also bore Hanumān on its banner.

words.root: śam (auspiciousness) + √kṛ, to make: 'one who brings blessing'
kesarin (maned one, lion; Hanumān's father) + nandana (√nand, to rejoice)
Skt. jagat ← √gam, to go ('that which moves')

meaning.en: Born of Śiva's essence, beloved son of Kesarī, your radiance and majesty are great, and the whole world bows to you.

bhava.en: Hanumān unites Śiva and Rāma. He is Śiva's own power given in service to Viṣṇu's avatāra, showing that devotion knows no sectarian walls.

notes: Many editions read 'शंकर स्वयं केसरीनंदन' (Śiva himself is Kesarī's son), reflecting the tradition that Hanumān is an avatāra of Rudra.

meaning.en: Learned, virtuous and exceedingly wise, you are always eager to do Rāma's work.

bhava.en: All his learning leads to one thing: eagerness to serve. Knowledge here is not hoarded; it is offered.

notes: In the Rāmāyaṇa, Rāma is struck by Hanumān's flawless speech at their first meeting and remarks that one who speaks so must have mastered the Vedas and grammar.

words.root: Skt. caritra ← √car, to move, to act
Skt. sītā, 'furrow'; she was found in a ploughed field

meaning.en: You delight in hearing the Lord's story; Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā dwell in your heart.

bhava.en: Hanumān is the great rasika: he never tires of Rāma's story. Tradition says that wherever the Rāmāyaṇa is recited, he is present, listening with folded hands.

notes: The traditional verse: 'yatra yatra raghunātha-kīrtanaṃ tatra tatra kṛta-mastakāñjalim…', meaning that wherever Rāma's glory is sung, there Hanumān stands with palms joined above his head and eyes full of tears.

meaning.en: Taking a tiny form, you appeared before Sītā; taking a fearsome form, you burned Laṅkā.

bhava.en: Small before the Mother, vast before arrogance. True strength knows when to become little.

notes: In the Sundara Kāṇḍa, Hanumān shrinks to the size of a cat (or smaller) to enter Laṅkā and appears to Sītā in the Aśoka grove.

words.root: Skt. saṃhāra: sam + √hṛ, to take away completely

meaning.en: Assuming a mighty form you destroyed the demons, and you accomplished every task of Rāmacandra.

bhava.en: Every form he takes, tiny or terrible, serves one purpose: Rāma's work. Nothing he does is for himself.

words.gloss: Śrī Rāma, hero of the Raghus

meaning.en: Bringing the Sañjīvanī herb, you revived Lakṣmaṇa, and Śrī Rāma, overjoyed, embraced you to his heart.

bhava.en: When he could not tell which herb was the right one, he brought the whole mountain. Love does not calculate; it brings everything.

notes: When Lakṣmaṇa fell to Meghanāda's weapon, Hanumān flew to the Himālaya for the herb and returned before dawn carrying the entire Droṇagiri peak.

lines.deva: तुम मम प्रिय भरतहि सम भाई ॥
lines.roman: Tum mam priya Bharatahi sam bhai

words.root: Skt. priya ← √prī, to please, to love

meaning.en: The Lord of the Raghus praised you greatly: 'You are as dear to me as my brother Bharata.'

bhava.en: Bharata is the model of perfect love for Rāma. To be called 'equal to Bharata' is the highest praise a devotee could receive, and it is spoken by the Lord himself.

words.gloss: Lord of Śrī (Lakṣmī), Rāma as Viṣṇu

meaning.en: 'May the thousand-mouthed (Śeṣa) sing your glory!' Saying this, the Lord of Śrī embraced you again.

bhava.en: Rāma's own words fail him. Only Śeṣa, the serpent with a thousand mouths, could sing Hanumān's praise, so Rāma simply embraces him.

meaning.en: Sanaka and the sages, Brahmā and the gods, the great munis, Nārada, Sarasvatī, and the lord of serpents…

bhava.en: Tulsidas assembles a heavenly choir: sages, creator, goddess of speech. Then, in the next verse, he admits even they fall short.

lines.deva: कबि कोबिद कहि सके कहाँ ते ॥
lines.roman: Kabi kobid kahi sake kahan te

meaning.en: …Yama, Kubera and the guardians of the directions: how could any of them, or any poet or scholar, fully describe your glory?

bhava.en: When the greatest beings run out of words, the poet's job becomes humility. Praise ends in wonder.

meaning.en: You did Sugrīva a great service: you brought him to Rāma and so gave him back his kingdom.

bhava.en: Hanumān's greatest gift to anyone is to bring them to Rāma. Everything else follows from that meeting.

meaning.en: Vibhīṣaṇa heeded your counsel and became lord of Laṅkā, as the whole world knows.

bhava.en: One good word at the right moment can change a destiny. Hanumān's meeting with Vibhīṣaṇa in Laṅkā set him on the path to Rāma.

words.root: Skt. yojana ← √yuj, to yoke: the distance covered in one yoking

meaning.en: The sun, thousands of yojanas away, you swallowed, thinking it was a sweet fruit.

bhava.en: The child Hanumān saw the rising sun and leapt for it, thinking it a ripe fruit. Even his mischief was so innocent and full of light that the gods could only marvel.

notes: Legend: Indra struck the child with his vajra on the jaw (hanu), and the name 'Hanumān' comes from this.

A popular modern reading multiplies the words: yuga (12,000) × sahasra (1,000) × yojana (≈8 miles) ≈ 96 million miles, close to the Earth–Sun distance (≈93 million miles). This is a devotional curiosity, not a traditional commentary.

words.root: jala (water) + dhi (√dhā, to hold): 'holder of waters'

meaning.en: Carrying the Lord's ring in your mouth, you leapt across the ocean. No wonder!

bhava.en: Why 'no wonder'? Because he carried Rāma's ring. With the Lord's name and token, the impossible becomes natural.

notes: Rāma gave Hanumān his signet ring to show Sītā as a sign of trust. It is still the emblem of a true messenger.

words.root: Skt. anugraha: anu + √grah, to take hold (of someone kindly)

meaning.en: However difficult the tasks of this world, by your grace they all become easy.

bhava.en: Durgam and sugam differ by one syllable. Grace changes 'hard to reach' into 'easy to reach' without changing the road.

meaning.en: You are the guardian at Rāma's door; no one enters without your permission.

bhava.en: To reach Rāma, go through Hanumān. The devotee becomes the doorway, which is why Hanumān shrines so often stand at the entrance to Rāma temples.

lines.deva: तुम रच्छक काहू को डर ना ॥
lines.roman: Tum rakshak kahu ko dar na

meaning.en: Whoever takes refuge in you obtains every joy. With you as protector, why fear anyone?

bhava.en: Śaraṇāgati, taking refuge, is the heart of bhakti. Fear does not disappear because danger is gone, but because a protector has come.

meaning.en: Only you can contain your own blazing power; at your roar all three worlds tremble.

bhava.en: Such power, held in such gentleness: that he can contain it is itself a sign of his mastery.

words.root: Skt. bhūta ← √bhū, to be ('that which has been')

meaning.en: Ghosts and evil spirits do not come near when the name of the great hero is spoken.

bhava.en: For centuries this verse has been whispered by frightened children in the dark. Fear of the unseen dissolves at his name.

meaning.en: Disease is destroyed and all pain removed by ceaselessly repeating the name of the hero Hanumān.

bhava.en: Nirantara means 'without a gap'. Healing comes from remembrance that runs unbroken beneath daily life.

notes: Tulsidas wrote another hymn, the Hanumān Bāhuk, when he was suffering severe pain in his arm, praying to Hanumān for relief.

lines.deva: मन क्रम बचन ध्यान जो लावै ॥
lines.roman: Man kram bachan dhyan jo lavai

meaning.en: Hanumān frees from distress whoever fixes their meditation on him in thought, deed and word.

bhava.en: Mind, action, speech: devotion is complete only when all three agree. This is why he is called Saṅkaṭa-mocana, the remover of distress.

lines.deva: तिन के काज सकल तुम साजा ॥
lines.roman: Tin ke kaj sakal tum saja

meaning.en: Rāma, the ascetic king, is supreme over all, and you accomplished all his works.

bhava.en: Rāma is both king and ascetic, ruling without attachment. Hanumān is the hands through which that dispassionate rule acts.

meaning.en: Whoever brings you any heart's desire obtains the boundless fruit of life.

bhava.en: Manoratha, the 'chariot of the mind': our desires carry us everywhere. Brought to Hanumān, that same chariot arrives at fulfilment beyond measure.

words.root: cf. Skt. ujjvala ← ud + √jval, to blaze

meaning.en: Your glory pervades all four ages; your fame is renowned as the light of the world.

bhava.en: Hanumān is a cirañjīvī, one of the 'long-lived' who remain on earth through the ages, so his glory is not only remembered but present.

words.root: Skt. sat ← √as, to be ('the real, the true')
ni + kanda (root, tuber): 'one who pulls up by the roots'

meaning.en: You are the protector of the good and the saints, the destroyer of demons, Rāma's darling.

bhava.en: Nikandana means to uproot. Hanumān does not trim evil; he removes it from the root. And yet to Rāma he is simply 'dulāre', a beloved child.

lines.deva: अष्ट सिद्धि नौ निधि के दाता ।
lines.roman: Ashta siddhi nau nidhi ke data

meaning.en: You are the giver of the eight siddhis and the nine treasures; Mother Jānakī granted you this boon.

bhava.en: Sītā, finding a son in the Aśoka grove, blessed him with every power to give away. Hanumān's wealth exists to be shared.

notes: The eight siddhis: aṇimā (becoming tiny), mahimā (vast), garimā (heavy), laghimā (light), prāpti (reaching anywhere), prākāmya (fulfilling any wish), īśitva (lordship), vaśitva (mastery).
In the Sundara Kāṇḍa, Sītā blesses him: 'अजर अमर गुननिधि सुत होहू', 'My son, may you be ageless, deathless, a treasury of virtues.'

words.gloss: of the Lord of the Raghus

meaning.en: You hold the elixir of Rāma's name; may you remain forever the servant of the Lord of the Raghus.

bhava.en: Hanumān could be anything, yet he chooses one identity: dāsa, servant. Dāsya bhakti, devotion as service, is his whole being.

notes: Some editions read 'सादर हो रघुपति के दासा', 'you are lovingly Rāma's servant'.

words.root: Skt. bhajana ← √bhaj, to share, partake, adore (the same root as bhakti)
Skt. duḥkha: duḥ (bad) + kha (axle-hole): a wheel that runs roughly

meaning.en: Through devotion to you one attains Rāma and leaves behind the sorrows of birth after birth.

bhava.en: Duḥkha literally pictures a badly fitted axle, life jolting along. Bhajan realigns the wheel.

words.root: hari (√hṛ, 'the one who takes away sin') + bhakta (√bhaj)

meaning.en: At life's end he goes to Rāma's own abode, and wherever he is born again, he is known as a devotee of Hari.

bhava.en: Even rebirth is not feared: the devotee asks only to be born again as a devotee.

meaning.en: Even one who does not keep other deities in mind attains every joy by serving Hanumān.

bhava.en: This is not a rejection of other gods but a reassurance: one sincere devotion is enough.

meaning.en: Distress is cut away and all pain vanishes for whoever remembers Hanumān, the mighty hero.

bhava.en: Smaraṇa, simple remembrance, is the easiest of the nine forms of bhakti, and here it is enough.

meaning.en: Victory, victory, victory to you, Lord Hanumān! Bless me with grace as my Guru would.

bhava.en: The hymn that began at the Guru's feet now asks Hanumān himself to be the Guru. The circle of grace closes.

notes: The threefold 'jai' is often sung with rising intensity and is a favourite moment in congregational singing.

lines.deva: जो सत बार पाठ कर कोई ।
lines.roman: Jo sat baar paath kar koi

meaning.en: Whoever recites this a hundred times is freed from bondage and attains great joy.

bhava.en: Bondage can mean a prison, as in the legend of the hymn's composition, or the subtler bondage of saṃsāra.

notes: Many editions read 'यह सत बार…', 'this, a hundred times'. Recitation 100 or 108 times is an established practice.

words.root: Skt. sākṣin: sa (with) + akṣi (eye), 'one who has seen'

meaning.en: Whoever reads this Hanumān Chālīsā attains perfection; Śiva, Lord of Gaurī, is the witness.

bhava.en: Śiva himself stands as sākṣī, witness, to this promise, fitting for a hymn to his own avatāra.

words.root: tulasī (holy basil, beloved of Viṣṇu) + dāsa (servant)

meaning.en: Tulsidas is forever Hari's servant. O Lord, make your dwelling in my heart.

bhava.en: The poet signs his name with the most intimate request of all. Not 'visit me' but 'camp here': make my heart your home.

notes: This is the 'signature verse' (chāp) customary in bhakti poetry, where the poet names himself.

lines.deva: पवनतनय संकट हरन मंगल मूरति रूप ।
lines.roman: Pavan-tanay sankat haran, mangal murati roop

words.root: Skt. mūrti ← √mūrch, to take solid shape

lines.deva: राम लखन सीता सहित हृदय बसहु सुर भूप ॥
lines.roman: Ram Lakhan Sita sahit, hriday basahu sur bhoop

meaning.en: O Son of the Wind, remover of distress, embodiment of all that is auspicious: king among the gods, dwell in my heart together with Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā.

bhava.en: The final wish is not for anything to be given but for someone to come: the whole divine family, living in one devotee's heart.

notes: Recitations often end with the call 'सियावर रामचंद्र की जय! पवनसुत हनुमान की जय!'

captions.c16: He brought Sugrīva to Rāma, and a kingdom was restored
captions.c17: In Laṅkā, a house marked with Rāma's name: Vibhīṣaṇa heeds his counsel
captions.c18: The child who leapt for the rising sun, thinking it a ripe fruit
captions.c19: With the Lord's ring in his mouth, he leapt across the ocean
captions.c20: By his grace the hardest tasks become easy: stones that float with Rāma's name
captions.c22: Take refuge in him, and what is there to fear?
captions.c23: Only he can hold his own blazing power; at his roar the three worlds tremble
captions.c24: Spirits of fear flee when the hero's name is spoken
captions.c25: Healing flows from his name, remembered without a gap
captions.c26: Mind, deed and word united in him: the remover of distress
captions.c27: Rāma, the ascetic king, rules over all; Hanumān carries out his every work
captions.c28: The chariot of the mind, brought to him, arrives at boundless fulfilment
captions.c29: His glory shines through all four ages: the light of the world
captions.c30: Protector of saints, uprooter of evil, Rāma's darling
captions.c31: Mother Jānakī's boon: giver of the eight powers and nine treasures
captions.c32: He holds the elixir of Rāma's name, forever the Lord's servant
captions.c33: Through bhajan, the jolting wheel of life runs true again
captions.c34: At the end, the journey home to Rāma's abode
captions.c36: Remember the mighty hero, and the chains of distress fall away
captions.c37: Jai, jai, jai! Be my Guru, Lord Hanumān
captions.c38: A hundred recitations: the prison opens, the bonds fall away
captions.c39: Śiva, Lord of Gaurī, stands witness
captions.c40: Tulsidas, forever Hari's servant: 'Lord, make my heart your home'
captions.d3: Dwell in my heart, with Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā
